name: libnpupnp
desc: C++ base UPnP library, derived from Portable UPnP, a.k.a libupnp
why: Opens the door to UPnP, the discovery protocol quietly running on nearly every home router and device.

brief.what_it_is: libnpupnp is a C++ library that implements the base UPnP protocol, derived from the older Portable UPnP library (pupnp, also called libupnp). It is the UPnP layer beneath the libupnpp C++ wrapper, which the upmpdcli and upplay applications use. The homepage describes it as a rewrite that keeps the UPnP-specific parts of the old code and swaps out its XML, HTTP server, and HTTP client components. The page does not spell out a full input and output contract, so the details of the API are not in these notes.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says the old libupnp had suffered for years from indifferent maintenance, with buggy releases shipped by Linux distributions. After contributing fixes and shipping a patched older release for several years, he concluded at the start of 2020 that the situation was unsalvageable and created libnpupnp (new pupnp) from the best parts of the old code.
brief.how_it_works: The custom ixml XML library is dropped in favour of expat, which parses XML when needed. The HTTP server and client are replaced by libmicrohttpd and libcurl. The retained code is converted to C++, with STL containers replacing the old hand-rolled lists and similar structures. The author reports that this cut the UPnP portion from about 24,000 lines of C to about 13,000 lines of C++.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no build or install commands. It says the upmpdcli and upplay packages can still be built against libupnpp 0.17.x and libupnp, while the default is now libupnpp 0.18.x with libnpupnp. Source is available as a tar archive on the upmpdcli downloads page and as a git repository, but the page does not give those URLs. No hardware, accounts, or runtime setup is mentioned on this page.
brief.standout: Rather than patching the old library again, the author rewrote it around well-maintained dependencies: expat for XML, libmicrohttpd for serving, and libcurl for client requests. The page reports a large reduction in code size, and the libupnpp layer lets applications switch underneath without changes.
brief.status: Quiet as far as these notes show. The homepage was last updated 2022-09-24. The page shows no release version, last commit date, or changelog, so current maintenance could not be confirmed from this page alone.
brief.caveats: The author says there is no chance the new library is free of bugs. There is no pure C interface yet; the author says one would be easy to add if someone wanted it, because the C++ interface comes from STL containers used at a few entry points. The page does not name a license. It also gives no install instructions and no usage examples, and the docs and git repository were not fetched, so the notes do not cover the API surface.
quotes: I came to the conclusion that the situation was unsalvageable, and, at the beginning of 2020, I created a new library, named libnpupnp (new pupnp), based of the best and most specific parts of the old code.
Of course there is no chance that the new library is free of bugs, but I think that they will be easier to find and fix than previously.
